prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Membrane fouling in protein-rich bioprocess streams has been characterized using resistance-in-series framework as a diagnostic tool, and Hermia blocking models fitted to flux–time data to diagnose mechanisms and inform cleaning protocol effectiveness.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-03384","field":"abstract","quote":"resistance-in-series framework as a diagnostic and modelling tool"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-02395","field":"abstract","quote":"Hermia's blocking models (complete, intermediate, standard blocking and cake filtration) were fitted to flux–time data"}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Industrial ultrafiltration systems use 10 and 30 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at TMP values of 0.5–3.0 bar for bioprocess clarification, and backwash at 0.5 bar for 30 s every 15 min restored 70–85% of initial flux.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02395","field":"abstract","quote":"10 and 30 kDa polyethersulphone membranes at TMP values of 0.5–3.0 bar"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-02395","field":"abstract","quote":"Backwash at 0.5 bar for 30 s every 15 min restored 70–85% of initial flux"}]}]}
